text:
Catalina and I collaborated on several backend projects at AdVerve, primarily focusing on scalable infrastructure and database optimization. Our interactions were frequent but informal, centered around shared goals like improving system reliability and reducing latency. She’s a steady presence in cross-functional meetings, often bridging engineering and product teams with clear, grounded insights.  

On a daily basis, Catalina tackles complex microservices architecture challenges, balancing PostgreSQL and MongoDB workloads to meet adtech demands. Her Terraform expertise shines in provisioning cloud resources—she once restructured our AWS cost model, trimming expenses without sacrificing performance. She’s equally comfortable debugging production issues or refining data pipelines, always prioritizing clarity over shortcuts.  

A standout moment came when she redesigned a legacy API to integrate with new AWS services, streamlining data flow across microservices. Her attention to detail ensured minimal downtime, and her ability to explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders was invaluable. She also mentored a junior engineer through a PostgreSQL optimization project, fostering a culture of shared growth.  

Catalina’s strength lies in her pragmatic approach to problem-solving and her knack for turning abstract system requirements into tangible, reliable solutions. She’s reliable, collaborative, and unafraid to ask critical questions—qualities that make her a trusted teammate in high-stakes environments.
